title: Tree Levels From the Bottom Up
statement:
Given the root of a binary tree, group its values by level. Return the levels starting from the deepest level and ending with the root's level.

Inside each level, values still go from left to right. An empty tree gives an empty list.

examples.why: The deepest level holds 4 (under 2) and 7 (under 8). Only the order of the levels flips; 4 still comes before 7.
A chain: one value per level, read from the bottom.

hints: First solve the usual top-down version: one list per level, root first. How would you get those?
Breadth-first search in rounds: at the start of each round the queue holds exactly one level.
Collect the levels top-down and reverse the outer list at the end. Do not reverse each inner list.

explain.intuition:
Levels come out naturally from the top: a queue processed in rounds of its current size hands you one level per round. Building them bottom-up directly is awkward, because you do not know how deep the tree is until you have seen it all.

So build them top-down and flip only the outer list at the end. Reversing L lists costs O(L), which is nothing next to visiting every node. Prepending each level to the front of an array instead would cost O(L) per level in JavaScript.
steps: If the root is null, return [].
Start a queue with the root.
While the queue is not empty, take exactly its current size of nodes, record their values in order, and push their children left then right.
Append that level's list to the result.
Reverse the result's outer list and return it.
pitfalls: Reversing every value instead of the order of the levels. Each level must still read left to right.
Pushing the right child before the left one, which reverses each level.
Using unshift per level. It works, but it is O(L) each time and turns a long chain into O(n²).

solutions.title: Depth-first with a depth index
solutions.idea: Walk the tree in preorder, carrying the depth. Append each value to the list for its depth, then reverse the list of lists.

solutions.title: Breadth-first, then reverse
solutions.idea: Process the queue one level per round, collect the levels top-down, and flip the outer list at the end.

followups: Return only the average of each level, still bottom-up.
Alternate the direction inside each level (left to right, then right to left). What changes?
